paragraphs: FS Bancorp, a Washington corporation, was organized in September 2011 for the purpose of becoming the holding company of 1st Security Bank upon the Bank's conversion from a mutual to a stock savings bank ("Conversion"). The Conversion was completed on July 9, 2012. At December 31, 2025, the Company had consolidated total assets of $3.2 billion, total loans receivable, net of $2.62 billion, total deposits of $2.67 billion, and total stockholders' equity of $307.7 million. The Company has not engaged in significant activities other than holding the stock of the Bank and providing capital to it through the debt and equity markets. Accordingly, the information set forth in this Form 10–K, including the consolidated financial statements and related data, relates primarily to the Bank.

1st Security Bank is a relationship-focused community bank dedicated to serving local families, regional businesses, and industry niches primarily within distinct Puget Sound and Pacific Northwest communities. The Bank prioritizes long-term relationships, working closely with customers to meet their financial needs while actively participating in community activities and events to further strengthen these connections.

1st Security Bank has been serving the Puget Sound area since 1907, including the period during which the predecessor to Anchor Bank, one of its banking acquisitions, was formed. The Bank was originally chartered as a credit union, under the name Washington's Credit Union and primarily served select employment groups. On April 1, 2004, the Bank converted from a credit union to a Washington state-chartered mutual savings bank. Upon completion of the Conversion in July 2012, 1st Security Bank became a Washington state-chartered stock savings bank and a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.

At December 31, 2025, the Company maintained its headquarters, which produces loans and accepts deposits, in Mountlake Terrace, Washington, and an administrative office in Aberdeen, Washington. The Bank also operates 27 full-service bank branches, of which 22 are located in Washington state and five in Oregon state, and 13 loan production offices in suburban communities in the greater Puget Sound and Pacific Northwest area. Among the 22 full-service branches in Washington, three are in Snohomish County, two in King County, two in Clallam County, two in Jefferson County, two in Pierce County, five in Grays Harbor County, two in Thurston County, two in Kitsap County, and two in Klickitat County. Furthermore, five full-service branches are located in Oregon: two in Lincoln County, two in Tillamook County, and one in Malheur County. Our 13 loan production offices include seven stand-alone offices: two in Pierce County, one in King County, one in Kitsap County, and one in Snohomish County in the Puget Sound region, as well as one in Benton County in Eastern Washington, and our newest office in Clark County, in Southwest Washington.

The Company is a diversified lender that specializes in originating various types of loans, including commercial real estate ("CRE"), multi-family, construction, one-to-four-family, and home equity loans, as well as consumer loans, such as indirect home improvement ("fixture secured loans"), and marine loans, along with commercial business loans. The Company's lending strategies aim to capitalize on new lending opportunities, arising from recent market consolidation, and focus on relationship lending. Retail deposits will remain a crucial funding source for the Company. For more detailed information about 1st Security Bank's business and operations, please refer to "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in this Form 10–K.

The Company has strategically pursued acquisitions, including whole bank acquisitions and branch purchases, to expand its customer base and enhance its distribution network. On February 24, 2023, the Company completed its purchase of seven retail bank branches from Columbia State Bank (the "Branch Acquisition"), adding approximately $425.5 million in deposits and $66.1 million in loans. The acquired branches are located in Goldendale and White Salmon, Washington, as well as Manzanita, Newport, Ontario, Tillamook, and Waldport, Oregon. The Branch Acquisition expanded our Puget Sound-focused retail footprint into southeastern Washington and Oregon, providing an opportunity to introduce its relationship-focused community banking model to these new markets.

1st Security Bank is examined and regulated by the Washington State Department of Financial Institutions ("DFI"), its primary regulator, and by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC"). 1st Security Bank is required to have certain reserves set by the Federal Reserve and is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines ("FHLB" or "FHLB of Des Moines"), which is one of the 11 regional banks in the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
The principal executive offices of the Company are located at 6920 220th Street SW, Mountlake Terrace, Washington 98043 and the main telephone number is (425) 771-5299.

As of December 31, 2025, the Company conducted operations from its headquarters, which provides both loan and deposit services, 13 loan production offices (seven of which were stand-alone), 27 full-service bank branches in the Puget Sound region of Washington, and various locations in Oregon.

The primary market area for business operations is the Seattle-Tacoma-Bellevue, Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area (the "Seattle MSA"), which includes King and Pierce Counties. The broader Puget Sound region consists of nine counties: King, Pierce, Snohomish, Kitsap, Lewis, Skagit, Island, Thurston, and Mason.

The Puget Sound region is the largest business center in both the State of Washington and the Pacific Northwest. It includes a highly developed urban core along Puget Sound surrounded by suburban residential and commercial areas and more rural communities in the north, east, and south.

The Puget Sound region's economy is diverse and supported by major industries, including aerospace, military installations, clean-energy technology, biotechnology, education, information technology, logistics, international trade, and tourism. Global and national industry leaders such as The Boeing Company, Microsoft, and Amazon.com play significant roles in driving regional economic activity. The area benefits from a highly educated workforce, a strong concentration of technology-oriented employment, and deep-water port facilities that support substantial international trade. Tourism is also an important contributor to the regional economy due to the area's natural beauty, temperate climate, and accessibility.

Within the nine-county Puget Sound region, four counties: King, Pierce, Snohomish, and Kitsap, constitute the Company's primary market area. King County, home to the city of Seattle, has the region's largest employment base and widest economic breadth, with major employers, including Microsoft, the University of Washington, Amazon.com, King County Government, Starbucks, and Costco. Pierce County, the region's second most populous county, features a diversified economy that includes military-related federal employment at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, significant healthcare providers such as MultiCare Health System and the Franciscan Health System, major shipping activity through the Port of Tacoma, and aerospace operations tied to Boeing.

Snohomish County's economy is anchored by aerospace manufacturing, including Boeing, as well as healthcare providers such as Providence Regional Medical Center, military presence at Naval Station Everett, and industries spanning biotechnology, electronics, and wood products. Kitsap County's economy is heavily influenced by the presence of the United States Navy, which is the county's largest employer with operations at Naval Base Kitsap, including the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard, Naval Undersea Warfare Center Keyport, Naval Submarine Base Bangor, and Naval Station Bremerton. Major private-sector employers in the county include St. Michael Medical Center/Franciscan Medical Group and Port Madison Enterprises.

headings: Risks Related to Macroeconomic Conditions
Our business may be adversely affected by downturns in the national economy and in the economies in our market areas.
Monetary policy, interest rate volatility, inflation, deflation, and other external economic factors could adversely impact our financial performance and operations.
Risks Related to our Lending Activities
Our loan portfolio possesses increased risk due to a large percentage of consumer loans.
Our business could suffer if we are unsuccessful in making, continuing, and growing relationships with home improvement contractors and dealers.
A significant portion of our business involves commercial real estate lending, which is subject to various risks that could adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Repayment of our commercial business loans is often dependent on the cash flows of the borrower, which may be unpredictable, and the collateral securing these loans may fluctuate in value.
Our residential construction lending is subject to various risks that could adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Our residential mortgage warehouse lending program is subject to various risks that could adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition.
If our ACL on loans is not sufficient to cover actual loan losses, our earnings could be reduced.
Our business may be adversely affected by credit risk associated with residential property.
Nonperforming assets take significant time to resolve and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition and could result in losses in the future.
Risk Related to Changes in Market Interest Rates
Changes in interest rates may reduce our net interest income and may result in higher defaults in a rising rate environment.
Our securities portfolio may be negatively impacted by fluctuations in market value and interest rates.
Risks Related to Accounting Matters
We may experience future goodwill impairment, which could reduce our earnings.
Our reported financial results depend on management's selection of accounting methods and certain assumptions and estimates, which, if incorrect, could cause unexpected losses in the future.
Risk Related to Regulatory and Compliance Matters
We may become subject to supervisory actions and enhanced regulation that could have a material adverse effect on our business, reputation, operating flexibility and financial condition.
Climate change and related legislative and regulatory initiatives may materially affect the Company's business and results of operations.
Non-compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act, Bank Secrecy Act, or other laws and regulations could result in fines or sanctions.
Risks Related to Cybersecurity, Data, Fraud, Third Parties and Technology
We rely on other companies to provide key components of our business infrastructure.
We are subject to certain risks in connection with our use of technology.
Our current and future uses of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies may create additional risks.
We are subject to certain risks in connection with our data management or aggregation.
Our business may be adversely affected by an increasing prevalence of fraud and other financial crimes.
Risks Related to Our Business and Industry Generally
Ineffective liquidity management could adversely affect our financial results and condition.
paragraphs: An investment in our common stock is subject to risks inherent in our business. Before making an investment decision, you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all the other information included in this report and our other documents filed with and furnished to the SEC. In addition to the risks and uncertainties described below, other risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, capital levels, cash flows, liquidity, results of operations, and prospects. The market price of our common stock could decline significantly due to any of these identified or other risks, and you could lose some or all your investment. The risks discussed below also include forward-looking statements, and our actual results may differ substantially from those discussed in these forward-looking statements. This report is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors.

Our primary market areas are in the Puget Sound region of Washington and Kitsap, Clallam, Jefferson, Grays Harbor, Thurston, and Benton counties. Following the acquisition of seven banking branches in 2023, our footprint expanded to include Klickitat County in Washington, and Lincoln, Malheur and Tillamook counties in Oregon. Adverse economic conditions in our market areas, including declining employment, reduced consumer spending, or business failures, could adversely affect our growth, customers' ability to repay loans, and consequently, our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Broader macroeconomic factors may also adversely affect our performance. Although inflation has moderated, higher input costs and persistent wage pressures continue to affect many borrowers, while the Federal Reserve's interest rate reductions in late 2025 have resulted in increased margin compression and reduced yields on adjustable- and variable-rate loans. Additionally, slowing economic activity, shifting consumer sentiment, and higher levels of household debt may negatively affect credit performance in our consumer and commercial portfolios. Trade disputes, tariffs, U.S. - China tensions, and shifting global supply chain patterns may continue to influence operating costs for our commercial borrowers, particularly those dependent on construction materials, manufacturing inputs, or exports.

A downturn in economic conditions, whether due to recessionary conditions, inflation or deflation, interest rate volatility, geopolitical conflicts, market instability, adverse weather events, or other factors, could have a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, and results of operations. Any of these conditions could lead to:
Reduced demand for our products and services, potentially leading to lower loan originations, deposits or other revenue.
Elevated loan delinquencies, nonperforming assets, and foreclosures.

paragraphs: This discussion and analysis reviews our consolidated financial statements and other relevant statistical data and is intended to enhance your understanding of our financial condition and results of operations. The information in this section has been derived from the Consolidated Financial Statements and footnotes thereto that appear in Item 8. of this Form 10–K. The information contained in this section should be read in conjunction with these Consolidated Financial Statements and footnotes and the business and financial information provided in this Form 10–K.

1st Security Bank has been serving the Puget Sound area since 1907, which includes the period in which the predecessor to Anchor Bank, one of its banking acquisitions, was formed. On July 9, 2012, the Bank converted from mutual to stock ownership and became the wholly owned subsidiary of FS Bancorp.

The Company is relationship-driven, delivering banking and financial services to local families, local and regional businesses and industry niches in suburban communities in the greater Puget Sound area, the Kennewick-Pasco-Richland metropolitan area of Washington, also known as the Tri-Cities, as well as Goldendale, Vancouver, and White Salmon, Washington and Manzanita, Newport, Ontario, Tillamook, and Waldport, Oregon.

The Company also maintains its long-standing indirect consumer lending platform which operates primarily throughout the Western United States. The Company emphasizes long-term relationships with families and businesses within the communities served, working with them to meet their financial needs. The Company is also actively involved in community activities and events within these market areas, which further strengthens its relationships within these markets.

The Company's strategic focus involves diversifying revenues, expanding lending channels, and enhancing the banking franchise. Management is committed to establishing varied revenue streams considering credit, interest rate, and concentration risks. The business plan includes:
Growing and diversifying our loan portfolio; Maintaining strong asset quality; Emphasizing lower cost core deposits to reduce the costs of funding our loan growth;

Capturing customers' complete relationships through a broad array of products and services, leveraging community involvement, and selectively emphasizing offerings aligned with customers' banking needs; and
As a diversified lender, the Company specializes in originating one-to-four-family residential loans, CRE mortgages, second mortgages, consumer loans, marine lending, and commercial business loans.

At December 31, 2025, the Company's loan portfolio consisted of the following major categories: CRE loans, residential real estate loans, consumer loans, and commercial business loans representing 36.5%, 28.6%, 22.5% and 12.4% of the portfolio, respectively.

Indirect home improvement loans to finance window, gutter, siding replacement, solar panels, spas, and other improvement renovations are a large segment of the consumer loan portfolio. These indirect home improvement loans are dependent on the Company's contractor/dealer network of 33 currently active fixture dealerships located throughout Washington, Oregon, California, Idaho, Colorado, Nevada, Arizona, Minnesota, Texas, Utah, Massachusetts, Montana, and New Hampshire. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company originated 6,146 indirect home improvement loans with an aggregate total of $138.2 million. Five contractor/dealer accounted for 77.5% of the dollar volume funded in this category. In addition, four states represented nearly three-quarters of the loan originations: Washington, Oregon, California, and Colorado with 37.0%, 19.0%, 12.9%, and 6.5% of total loan volume, respectively.

The Company originates one-to-four-family residential mortgage loans through referrals from real estate agents, financial planners, builders, and from existing customers. Retail banking customers are also an important source of the Company's loan originations. The Company originated $716.6 million of one-to-four-family loans (which included loans held for sale, loans held for investment and fixed seconds) in addition to $22.9 million of loans brokered to other institutions through the home lending segment during the year ended December 31, 2025, of which $555.2 million were sold to investors. Of the loans sold to investors, $209.1 million were sold to the FNMA, FHLMC, FHLB, and GNMA with servicing rights retained for the purpose of further developing these customer relationships.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, one-to-four-family loan originations and refinancing activity increased compared to the prior period as a result of changes in interest rates and economic conditions. Residential construction and development lending, while not as common as other loan origination options like one-to-four-family loans, continues to be an important element in our total loan portfolio, and we continue to take a disciplined approach by concentrating our efforts on loans to builders and developers in our market areas known to us. These short-term loans typically have a maturity period of six to 18 months, with disbursements not fully realized at origination, leading to a short-term reduction in net loans receivable.

The Company is affected by prevailing economic conditions, as well as government policies and regulations concerning, among other things, monetary and fiscal affairs. Deposit flows are influenced by a number of factors, including interest rates paid on time deposits, other investments, account maturities, and the overall level of personal income and savings. Lending activities are influenced by the demand for funds, the number and quality of lenders, and regional economic cycles. Sources of funds for lending activities include primarily deposits, including brokered deposits, borrowings, payments on loans, and income provided from operations.

The Company's earnings are primarily dependent upon net interest income, the difference between interest income and interest expense. Interest income is a function of the balances of loans and investments outstanding during a given period and the yield earned on these loans and investments. Interest expense is a function of the amount of deposits and borrowings outstanding during the same period and the interest rates paid on these deposits and borrowings.

paragraphs: FS Bancorp, 一間華盛頓州公司, 於 2011 年 9 月設立, 目的為成為 1st Security Bank 的控股公司, 以該銀行從合夥制轉為股份制儲蓄銀行 ("轉換")。轉換於 2012 年 7 月 9 日完成。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日, 本公司合併總資產為 3.2 十億美元, 網路貸款應收款為 2.62 十億美元, 總存款為 2.67 十億美元, 以及總股東權益為 307.7 百萬美元。本公司除持有銀行股票及透過債券及股權市場提供資金外, 未從事其他重大活動。因此, 本 Form 10–K 所載資訊, 包括合併財務報表及相關資料, 主要與銀行有關。
1st Security Bank 是一家以關係為導向的社區銀行, 致力服務當地家庭、區域性企業及產業專業領域, 主要服務於不同的普吉特海灣及太平洋西北地區社區。該銀行優先考量長期關係, 並與客戶密切合作以滿足其財務需求, 同時積極參與社區活動及事件以進一步強化這些聯繫。

1st Security Bank 自 1907 年開始服務普吉特海灣地區, 包括其前身 Anchor Bank, 一家其銀行收購之一, 的成立時期。該銀行最初以信用合作社形式註冊, 名稱為 Washington's Credit Union, 主要服務特定就業羣組。於 2004 年 4 月 1 日, 該銀行從信用合作社轉為華盛頓州註冊的合夥制儲蓄銀行。於 2012 年 7 月轉換完成後, 1st Security Bank 成為華盛頓州註冊的股份制儲蓄銀行, 並為本公司之 wholly-owned subsidiary。

於 2025 年 12 月 31 日, 本公司維持其總部, 用以發放貸款及接受存款, 位於華盛頓州 Mountlake Terrace, 並設有位於華盛頓州 Aberdeen 的行政辦公室。該銀行亦運作 27 間全功能銀行分行, 其中 22 間位於華盛頓州, 5 間位於俄勒岡州, 並設有 13 間貸款發放辦公室, 位於普吉特海灣及太平洋西北地區的郊區社區。其中華盛頓州的 22 間全功能分行, 3 間位於 Snohomish 縣, 2 間位於 King 縣, 2 間位於 Clallam 縣, 2 間位於 Jefferson 縣, 2 間位於 Pierce 縣, 5 間位於 Grays Harbor 縣, 2 間位於 Thurston 縣, 2 間位於 Kitsap 縣, 以及 2 間位於 Klickitat 縣。此外, 俄勒岡州有 5 間全功能分行: 2 間位於 Lincoln 縣, 2 間位於 Tillamook 縣, 以及 1 間位於 Malheur 縣。我們的 13 間貸款發放辦公室包括 7 間獨立辦公室: 2 間位於 Pierce 縣, 1 間位於 King 縣, 1 間位於 Kitsap 縣, 1 間位於 Snohomish 縣的普吉特海灣地區, 以及 1 間位於 Eastern Washington 的 Benton 縣, 並設有我們在 Southwest Washington 的 Clark 縣的最新辦公室。

本公司是一家多元化貸款機構, 專門發放各種類型的貸款, 包括商業不動產 ("CRE"), 多家庭住宅, 建築貸款, 一至四家庭住宅, 以及住宅抵押貸款, 以及消費者貸款, 如間接住宅改善貸款 ("裝置抵押貸款"), 以及船舶貸款, 以及商業企業貸款。本公司的貸款策略旨在把握因近期市場合併而產生的新貸款機會, 並專注於關係貸款。零售存款將繼續是本公司重要的資金來源。如需更多關於 1st Security Bank 的業務及運作詳細資訊, 請參閱本 Form 10–K 中的 "Item 7. 管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之分析"。

本公司已戰略性地進行收購, 包括整體銀行收購及分行買斷, 以擴大客戶羣及強化分銷網路。於 2023 年 2 月 24 日, 本公司完成從 Columbia State Bank ("分行買斷") 收購 7 間零售銀行分行, 增加約 425.5 百萬美元存款及 66.1 百萬美元貸款。所收購的分行位於華盛頓州的 Goldendale 及 White Salmon, 以及俄勒岡州的 Manzanita, Newport, Ontario, Tillamook, 以及 Waldport。此分行買斷將我們以普吉特海灣為重點的零售業務拓展至華盛頓州東南及俄勒岡州, 提供機會將我們以關係為導向的社區銀行模式引入這些新市場。
1st Security Bank 由華盛頓州財政機構部門 ("DFI") 考核及監管, 並為其主要監管機構, 以及由美國存款保險公司 ("FDIC") 監管。1st Security Bank 需要符合聯邦儲備局所設定的特定準備金, 並為聯邦住宅貸款銀行 ("FHLB") 會員, 這是聯邦住宅貸款銀行系統中的 11 家區域銀行之一。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司於其總部進行營運，該總部提供貸款與存款服務，並設有 13 處貸款業務辦公室（其中 7 處為獨立營運），27 處全功能銀行分行位於華盛頓州的普吉特海灣地區，以及 Oregon 省的多處據點。
本公司營運的主要市場區域為華盛頓州西雅圖-塔科馬-貝爾維尤都會區（簡稱 "西雅圖都會區"），該都會區包含 King 縣與 Pierce 縣。較廣義的普吉特海灣地區則包含九個縣：King、Pierce、Snohomish、Kitsap、Lewis、Skagit、Island、Thurston 與 Mason。
普吉特海灣地區為華盛頓州與太平洋西北地區最大的商業中心。該地區包含高度發達的都市核心，沿著普吉特海灣分佈，周圍則為市郊住宅與商業區，以及北部、東部與南部較為鄉村的社區。

普吉特海灣地區的經濟多元，並由主要產業支撐，包括航空太空、軍事設施、潔淨能源技術、生物科技、教育、資訊科技、物流、國際貿易與旅遊業。全球與國家級產業領導者，如 The Boeing Company、Microsoft 與 Amazon.com，在推動區域經濟活動上扮演重要角色。該地區受益於高素質的勞動力、強大的科技導向就業集中度，以及深水港口設施，支持大量國際貿易。旅遊業也是區域經濟的重要貢獻者，因該地區擁有自然美景、溫和氣候與良好的交通便利性。

在九個縣組成的普吉特海灣地區中，King、Pierce、Snohomish 與 Kitsap 四個縣為本公司的主要市場區域。King 縣為西雅圖市所在地，擁有該地區最大的就業基礎與最廣的經濟範圍，主要僱主包括 Microsoft、華盛頓大學、Amazon.com、King 縣政府、Starbucks 與 Costco。Pierce 縣為該地區人口第二多的縣，經濟多元化，包括位於 Joint Base Lewis-McChord 的軍事相關聯邦就業、重要的醫療機構如 MultiCare Health System 與 Franciscan Health System、透過 Tacoma 港口的重大貨運活動，以及與 Boeing 有關的航空太空產業。

Snohomish 縣的經濟以航空太空製造業為主，包括 Boeing，以及醫療機構如 Providence Regional Medical Center，軍事設施如 Naval Station Everett，以及生物技術、電子產品與木材製品等產業。Kitsap 縣的經濟深受美國海軍的影響，該海軍為該縣最大的僱主，於 Naval Base Kitsap 進行運作，包括 Puget Sound Naval Shipyard、Naval Undersea Warfare Center Keyport、Naval Submarine Base Bangor 與 Naval Station Bremerton。該縣的主要私人部門僱主包括 St. Michael Medical Center/Franciscan Medical Group 與 Port Madison Enterprises。

paragraphs: 本討論與分析審閱我們的合併財務報表及其他相關統計資料，旨在增進您對我們財務狀況與營運成果的瞭解。本節資訊係根據本 Form 10–K 第 8 項所載之合併財務報表及其附註資料整理而成。請配合閱讀本節資訊與上述合併財務報表及其附註資料，以及本 Form 10–K 所提供的業務與財務資訊。
1st Security Bank 自 1907 年起服務 Puget Sound 區域，包含其後成為 Anchor Bank（為其銀行收購之一）前身所成立之期間。2012 年 7 月 9 日，該銀行從合作制轉為股份制，成為 FS Bancorp 的 wholly owned subsidiary。

本公司以關係為導向，為當地家庭、當地及區域性企業與產業專業領域提供銀行與財務服務，服務範圍包括 Puget Sound 大區的郊區社區、華盛頓州的 Kennewick-Pasco-Richland 大都會區，亦稱為 Tri-Cities，以及華盛頓州的 Goldendale、Vancouver 與 White Salmon，以及俄勒岡州的 Manzanita、Newport、Ontario、Tillamook 與 Waldport。
本公司亦維持其長期的間接消費者貸款平台，主要運作於美國西部地區。本公司強調與所服務社區內的家庭與企業建立長期關係，協助他們滿足財務需求。本公司亦積極參與這些市場區域的社區活動與事件，進一步強化其在這些市場的關係。
本公司戰略重點包括多元化收入來源、擴展貸款渠道，以及提升銀行品牌。管理階層致力於建立多元化的收入來源，考量信貸、利率與集中風險。業務計畫包含：
擴大並多元化貸款組合；維持強勁的資產品質；強調低成本的核心存款以降低貸款成長的資金成本；
透過廣泛的產品與服務來捕捉客戶的完整關係，善用社區參與，並選擇性強調符合客戶銀行需求的服務項目；以及
作為一家多元化貸款機構，本公司專注於發放一至四戶住宅貸款、商業不動產抵押貸款、二次抵押貸款、消費者貸款、船舶貸款以及商業企業貸款。
於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司貸款組合包含以下主要類別：商業不動產貸款、住宅不動產貸款、消費貸款及商業貸款，分別佔組合的 36.5%、28.6%、22.5% 和 12.4%。

間接住宅改善貸款用以資助窗戶、排水管、外牆板、太陽能板、水療設施及其它改善工程，為消費貸款組合的重要部分。這些間接住宅改善貸款依賴於本公司 33 家目前活躍的裝修商/經銷商網路，分佈於華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、加利福尼亞州、愛達荷州、科羅拉多州、內華達州、亞利桑那州、明尼蘇達州、德克薩斯州、猶他州、馬薩諸塞州、蒙大拿州及新罕布夏州。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度，本公司發放了 6,146 筆間接住宅改善貸款，總金額為 138.2 百萬美元。五家裝修商/經銷商在該類別的資金投放中佔 77.5%。此外，四個州代表了近七成的貸款發放：華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、加利福尼亞州及科羅拉多州，分別佔總貸款金額的 37.0%、19.0%、12.9% 和 6.5%。

本公司透過房地產經紀、財務規劃師、建築師及現有客戶的推薦發放一至四戶住宅抵押貸款。零售銀行客戶也是本公司貸款發放的重要來源。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度，本公司發放了一至四戶住宅貸款 716.6 百萬美元（包含待售貸款、待投資貸款及固定二套房貸款），並透過住宅貸款業務發放了 22.9 百萬美元貸款至其他機構，其中 555.2 百萬美元已出售給投資者。在出售給投資者的貸款中，209.1 百萬美元已出售給 FNMA、FHLMC、FHLB 及 GNMA，並保留服務權以進一步發展這些客戶關係。

於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度，一至四戶住宅貸款發放及重新貸款活動較前一時期增加，這是因應利率變動及經濟條件的改變所致。住宅建設及開發貸款，雖然不如一至四戶住宅貸款等其他貸款發放選項常見，但仍為本公司總貸款組合的重要組成部分，本公司持續採用嚴謹的策略，專注於我們所熟悉的市場區域中對建築師及開發商的貸款。這些短期貸款通常有六至十八個月的償還期限，貸款發放時資金並未完全到位，導致短期內淨貸款應收款減少。
本公司受總體經濟條件及政府政策與規範的影響，包括貨幣及財政事務等。存款流動受多種因素影響，包括定期存款的利率、其他投資、帳戶到期日及個人收入與儲蓄的總體水平。貸款活動受資金需求、貸款人數量與品質及區域經濟週期的影響。貸款活動的資金來源主要包括存款（包括經紀存款）、借款、貸款償還及營運所得。
本公司獲利主要取決於淨利息收入，即利息收入與利息支出的差額。利息收入取決於特定期間內貸款與投資的餘額及這些貸款與投資的收益率。利息支出取決於特定期間內存款與借款的餘額及這些存款與借款的利率。

headings: 與總體經濟條件相關的風險
本公司業務可能因國家經濟及我們所處市場區域經濟衰退而受到不利影響。
貨幣政策、利率波動、通貨膨脹、通貨收縮及其他外部經濟因素可能對本公司財務表現及營運造成不利影響。
與本公司貸款業務相關的風險
本公司貸款組合因消費者貸款佔比高而具備較高風險。
若本公司未能成功建立、維持並拓展與住宅改善承包商及經銷商的關係，本公司業務可能受到影響。
本公司業務有相當大一部分涉及商業不動產貸款，此類貸款面臨多種風險，可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司商業貸款的償還通常取決於借款人現金流，而現金流可能難以預測，且用以擔保這些貸款的抵押品價值可能波動。
本公司住宅建築貸款業務面臨多種風險，可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司住宅房貸倉儲貸款計畫面臨多種風險，可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
若本公司貸款應提備的貸款減損準備不足以涵蓋實際貸款減損，將可能導致本公司獲利減少。
本公司業務可能因住宅不動產相關信用風險而受到不利影響。
不良資產需要相當長的時間才能解決，並對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響，未來亦可能導致損失。
與市場利率變動相關之風險
利率變動可能降低本公司淨利息收入，並在利率上升環境中導致更高的違約率。
本公司證券投資組合可能因市場價值波動及利率變動而受到負面影響。
會計事項相關風險
我們可能遭遇未來 goodwill 損失，這可能會降低我們的營業收入。
我們的財務結果報告依賴管理階層選擇會計方法及某些假設與估計，若這些假設與估計不正確，可能會導致未來出現意外損失。
與監管及合規事項相關的風險
我們可能面臨監督機構的處分及更嚴格的監管，這可能會對我們的業務、聲譽、營運彈性及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
氣候變遷及相關的立法與監管措施可能對本公司業務及營運成果造成重大影響。
未遵守 USA PATRIOT Act、Bank Secrecy Act 或其他法律法規，可能會導致處罰或制裁。
與網路安全、資料、詐欺、第三方及科技相關的風險
本公司依賴其他公司提供業務基礎建設的關鍵零組件。
本公司因使用科技而面臨某些風險。
本公司目前及未來使用人工智慧（AI）及其他新興科技，可能產生額外風險。
本公司因資料管理或資料彙整而面臨某些風險。
本公司可能因詐欺及其他財務犯罪事件日益普遍而受到不利影響。
與本公司業務及產業相關的一般風險
流動性管理不當可能對本公司財務結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股有風險，這些風險與本公司業務本質有關。在做出投資決定前，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本報告及本公司其他提交至美國證券交易委員會（SEC）之文件中所包含的所有資訊。除下列所描述的風險與不確定性外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不重要，但這些風險與不確定性可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、資本水準、現金流、流動性、營運成果與前景產生重大且不利的影響。本公司普通股的市場價格可能因任何這些已識別或其它風險而顯著下跌，您可能損失部分或全部投資。下列所討論的風險也包含前瞻性陳述，而本公司實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述中所討論的結果有顯著差異。本報告全部內容均受這些風險因素所限制。
本公司主要市場區域位於華盛頓州的普吉特聲地區及基斯卡普、克利拉姆、傑斐遜、格雷厄姆海灣、瑟圖斯頓與本頓縣。在2023年收購七家銀行分行後，本公司業務範圍擴展至華盛頓州的克利卡提縣，以及俄勒岡州的林肯、馬勒和提拉穆克縣。若本公司市場區域出現不利的經濟條件，包括就業率下降、消費者支出減少或企業破產，可能會對本公司成長、客戶償還貸款的能力，以及進而對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。

更廣泛的總體經濟因素也可能對本公司表現產生不利影響。雖然通貨膨脹已趨緩，但較高的投入成本與持續的工資壓力仍影響許多借款人，而聯邦儲備理事會在2025年底的利率減降導致利差收縮增加，以及可調息與變動利率貸款的收益率下降。此外，經濟活動減緩、消費者情緒轉變，以及較高的家庭債務水平，可能對本公司消費性與商業貸款組合的信用表現產生負面影響。貿易爭議、關稅、美國與中國關係緊張，以及全球供應鏈模式的變化，可能持續影響本公司商業借款人的營運成本，特別是那些依賴建設材料、製造投入或出口的借款人。
若經濟條件出現衰退，無論是因經濟衰退、通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮、利率波動、地緣政治衝突、市場不穩定、不利天氣事件或其他因素，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大不利影響。任何這些條件都可能導致：
本公司產品與服務的需求減少，可能導致貸款發放、存款或其他收入減少。
貸款違約率上升、非表現貸款資產與財產拍賣增加。
